edit.description: The home. `drift::to_lock_path` (&Path -> String) and its `normalize_lock_path` (&str -> String) move here — the module that already declares this canonical form on `HarnessRelativePath` (113: '/-separated, no leading ./, normalized') — and are named for the spelling rather than the lock, since diagnostics and locus patterns are consumers now. `relativize_against_root`'s own two inline `replace('\\', "/")` (83, 96) route through the one home.

`to_lock_path` (994) and `normalize_lock_path` (1004) leave for `path`; every caller keeps calling the one home. `emit_owned_targets_from_doc` (4288) spells `EmitOwnedEntry.path` through it — today the path is `PathBuf::from` the raw row while only the `collected` dedupe beside it normalizes, so an older lock's `./CLAUDE.md` reaches `install` un-canonicalized against `specs/model/pipeline.md`, 'The lock' ('older spellings normalize at read time'). The `to_lock_path_normalizes_a_backslash_joined_path` unit test (6436) moves with the function.

Four hand-rolls fold onto the one home: `path_matches`'s candidate side (1538) — the left side canonicalizes through `harness_relative` and the right only `/`-separates, so an older lock's `./x` row matches no candidate and the guard binds nothing; `harness_relative`'s own tail (1551); `projection_owner_line` (1582); and the two manifest diagnostics (1791, 1817). The stale `PATH-SEP-NORMALIZE` cite in the three doc comments at 1526/1543/1556 resolves nowhere at HEAD and is re-pointed at the one home as this entry opens the file.
The `GuardedLocus.pattern` spelling (865) folds onto the one home.
`repo_file_set`'s entry spelling (1713) folds onto the one home. This module's test-side expectation spellings (2030, 2031, 2054, 2058, 2118) stay hand-rolled on purpose.

The regression the fold closes: a projection whose lock row carries the older `./` spelling binds the guard. Sits beside `guard_matches_a_projection_by_path_equality_not_suffix` (2440) and `guard_reaches_the_same_verdict_from_a_dot_root_as_from_an_absolute_root` (2581).
Only if the `./`-spelled row needs a fixture face; a hand-written lock inside the test is preferred over widening `GuardLock`.
Declared for the fence; a canonical lock renders identically, so no change is expected.
Declared for the fence; the gauntlet lock carries no `./` row, so no change is expected.

summary: The `/`-separated, `./`-less path spelling gets one home in src/path.rs — ten production hand-rolls fold onto it, closing a guard that misses an older lock's `./x` row.

tests.asserts: a lock whose provenance row spells `./CLAUDE.md` binds the guard: a `PreToolUse` write to that projection is refused with the owner line, where today the un-normalized candidate matches no relativized `file_path` and the write passes unchecked. Fails on the pre-fix tree.

the one home `/`-separates a backslash-joined path and erases a leading `./` (the moved `to_lock_path_normalizes_a_backslash_joined_path`, extended with the `./` case `normalize_lock_path`'s doc cites decision 0024 for).

acceptance: `cargo test` green with the new guard-binding case, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean, and no production `replace('\\', "/")` left outside src/path.rs.
notes: Census is by behavior: 10 production sites. The 10 test-side copies (src/compose.rs tests, tests/it/{bundle,gauntlet,directive_classing}.rs) stay hand-rolled — an expectation that borrows the implementation's normalizer stops asserting the spelling. Overlaps the parked LOCK-DECLARATION-CODEC-GETS-ITS-OWN-MODULE in src/drift.rs: this fold shrinks that split's scope by two functions rather than colliding with it. scoped at 06209dfe
